A pre-prepared or memorised composition will earn you no marks. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. Time allowed: two hours.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION B - COMPOSITION (40 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organisation (12 marks); Expression (16 marks); Accuracy (12 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write on from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity (e.g. your name, school, parentage etc). You should write between 450 - 500 words.

questions.enonce_markdown: **e)** Electricity has just been installed in your locality. How has this affected life in your area?
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Introduction: life before electricity and the day it arrived.
2. Effects on business and employment.
3. Effects on education.
4. Effects on health and security.
5. Problems (bills, power cuts, laziness), personal opinion and conclusion.

**Model composition (457 words)**

The day electricity reached our village was a day we shall never forget. For years we had lived in darkness after sunset, depending on kerosene lamps, candles and the moon. When engineers planted the poles and strung the cables along the road, children followed them in excitement, and on the evening the lights were switched on, the whole village gathered in the square and clapped. Since then, life in our area has changed in many ways, most of them for the better.

The most obvious change is in the economy. Small businesses have multiplied. Mr. Njoh, the local tailor, now uses an electric sewing machine and finishes in one day what once took him three. Hairdressers have opened salons with dryers and clippers, and a young man has started a phone-charging and photocopying business that earns him a good income. Welders and carpenters use machines that save time, and the village mill grinds maize and cassava faster than ever. Shop owners sell cold drinks and fresh fish because they can now keep them in refrigerators. As a result, many young people have found jobs in the village instead of drifting to the cities.

Education has also benefited. Students can now study at night under bright bulbs, without the smoke that used to irritate their eyes. Our school has bought a computer and a photocopier, and teachers prepare their lessons more easily. Some pupils watch educational programmes on television and listen to the news on the radio, which improves their knowledge of the world. In the last public examinations, more pupils from our school passed than ever before.

Health care has improved as well. The health centre can now keep vaccines and medicines at the right temperature and offer treatment after dark. Mothers no longer fear giving birth at night in a poorly lit ward. Furthermore, street lights have made our roads safer, and the number of thefts and accidents at night has fallen.

However, electricity has brought some problems. Many families cannot pay their monthly bills, and some have started to use illegal connections, which are dangerous and have caused fires. Power cuts are frequent and sometimes damage appliances. Some young people now spend whole nights watching films and football instead of sleeping or revising, and a few have become lazy. Moreover, the cost of living in the village has risen slightly, because landlords have increased their rents.

In my opinion, the advantages far outweigh the disadvantages. To enjoy the benefits fully, the community should use electricity wisely, pay bills regularly, and report any dangerous wires to the authorities. The government should also ensure that the supply is stable. If we do these things, electricity will continue to light not only our homes, but also our future.

**Marking grid**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organisation | 12 | Relevant ideas that answer the topic, developed with examples, in clear paragraphs with an introduction and a conclusion |
| Expression | 16 | Varied vocabulary and sentence structures, appropriate style and tone, fluent links between ideas |
| Accuracy | 12 | Correct grammar, tenses, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. Listing advantages only, with no examples from the writer's own locality.
2. Writing about how electricity works (a science essay) instead of its effect on life in the area.
